label: prop:sl2-period-conserved-quantity
title: The depth-2 prolongation recurrence has a conserved first integral
html:
The one-parameter recurrence (prop:sl2-prolongation-recurrence)

a_D^{(n+2)} = \tau\,a_D^{(n+1)} - a_D^{(n)},
\qquad \tau = \mathrm{tr}\, B,\ \det B = 1,

on the prolonged Seiberg--Witten periods admits a conserved first integral — the discrete energy of the Lucas/Chebyshev orbit, equivalently the cup-product symplectic form evaluated on consecutive periods:

\boxed{\;
H_n := \bigl(a_D^{(n+1)}\bigr)^2 - \tau\,a_D^{(n+1)}a_D^{(n)} + \bigl(a_D^{(n)}\bigr)^2
\quad\text{satisfies}\quad H_{n+1} = H_n
\;}

so H_n = H_0 for every n. The invariant exists because \det B = 1: it is the quadratic form fixed by B \in \mathrm{SL}_2 acting on (a_D^{(n)}, a_D^{(n+1)}).

Fork consequence (the depth-2 hypothesis is the n\le 4 germ). A genuine depth-2, \det = 1 orbit keeps H_n constant; in the hyperbolic case \tau = 2\cosh\theta > 2 the conic H_n = H_0 forces the ratio a_D^{(n+1)}/a_D^{(n)} to a fixed limit \lambda_+ = e^{\theta} (geometric growth). But the true prolonged period is the residue sum (prop:sw-period-residue-sum) a_D^{(n)} = \sum_{\lambda} \dim_q, a per-block Wedderburn quantum-dimension sum that grows factorially (super-exponentially), so its ratio a_D^{(n+1)}/a_D^{(n)} is unbounded and H_n \to \infty. A factorial sequence conserves no first integral, hence satisfies no depth-2 recurrence: the \tau fitted from three residue weights \tau = (a_D^{(2)} + a_D^{(4)})/a_D^{(3)} is an effective germ matching n\le 4, not the period recurrence. The exact prolongation kernel is the q-Bessel-class q-difference operator of the super-exponential residue sum (prop:binding-genfun-qdifference), not a 2\times 2 Cayley--Hamilton relation.
